frame: chair frame mm: +x = chair's right, +y = forward, +z = up, table at z = 0

observed.method: orthophotos of each arm's top over its front leg, 0.2 mm/px, plane fitted to the model arm top (tools/arm_top_ortho.py, model v13); left arm: 12 of 15 photos within 60 deg show it; right arm: 15 photos, none show anything

left_arm_oval.what: a darker oval on the LEFT arm top, long axis along the arm's grain (fore-aft); the one seen in IMG_1528
left_arm_oval.position_note: not over the leg's centre: it sits at the leg's front-outer corner and mostly in front of it, about 14 mm outboard of the model leg's centreline and 20-28 mm forward of its top centre (the leg rakes, so the two views differ by ~8 mm). Its outer edge is ~4 mm outside the leg's outer face. The model front leg is placed right: its front edge matches the side photos within ~3 mm.

observed.right_arm: nothing visible at the matching place or anywhere over the leg (15 photos, IMG_1476-1549)

arm_front_leg.reading: not a through-tenon: a tenon from the leg would sit over the leg's top, would show on both arms, and its end grain would be roughly as long across as along. The oval is most likely a feature of the board (a filled knot or patch) on the left arm only. The joint between arm and front leg is therefore HIDDEN.

design.kind: blind 10 mm Domino, vertical along the leg axis, centred on the leg top's contact face with the arm underside, long axis fore-aft
design.provenance: ASSUMED: the builder uses 10 mm Dominos at the seat (parts/dominos.json); the arm is ~25 mm thick (parts/arms.json, assumed), so 15 mm in leaves 10 mm of arm above it. A short round tenon would fit the photos equally well; it changes no template outline.

back_leg_rear.what: Hub, Joe's fix list item 1 (IMG_1620, from behind). Each back leg shows THREE Domino ends: (a) on its OUTER face at the seat (parts/dominos.json back_leg, already modelled as DOMINO_B*, confirmed in IMG_1508); (b) on its REAR face at seat height, across the seam between the leg's inner face and the seat's back edge; (c) on its REAR face at arm height, centred on the leg's width. This block is (b) and (c).

observed.method: orthophotos of each back leg's rear face in two windows, on the plane fitted to the model leg's rear face there (tools/rear_ortho.py, model v16; fit 0.34-0.35 mm rms), then 0.1 mm/px tiles of each Domino end with its edges taken at the steepest tone change (tools/rear_dominos/measure.py). Each tip triangulated from its readings in 3 to 6 photos (tools/rear_dominos/tri.py). IMG_1620 itself did not register (close-up); the registered photos from behind (IMG_1499-1504, 1512-1513, 1578, 1491) show every end.

visible_end_mm.note: left: IMG_1578 (close-up), the end runs from plane u +7.8 to +32.4 (|x| 198.95 to 174.35) read to the outside of its rim; right: its seat-side tip is dark on dark, soft
visible_end_mm.seat_side_tip: soft: on the seat's side the dark end has a lighter rim 1-2 mm wide (the Domino's rounded end catching the light, or glue). The steepest tone change sits on the rim's inside (u +31.3 in 1578, +31.4 in 1501), its outside at u +32.4 in 1578. In the more distant photos (IMG_1502) the rim blurs outward and the end looks about 26 mm long

leg_side_tip_xyz.note: 1.3 mm (left) and 0.6 mm (right) in front of the model leg's rear face: on the face

seam_mm_of_the_end_in_the_leg.note: the seam between the leg's inner face and the seat is visible across the Domino end; about 10 mm of the end is in the seat

visible_end_mm.note: tip to tip from the two triangulated tips

arm.on_the_leg: the model leg's rear face is centred on |x| 211.2 at that height: the Domino is centred on the leg's width. The tips sit -0.7 to +1.7 mm off the model's rear face
arm.through_to_the_arm: a Domino driven in square to the rear face (17.5 degrees up from level) leaves the leg's front face at z about 492, the middle of the model arm's end (z 480-508): consistent with the arm as modelled

design.note: symmetric (left/right mean). tools/joinery.py places each Domino ON the model leg's rear face at 'centre_abs_x', 'centre_z', long axis level, and drives it in square to that face.

seat.kind: 10 mm Domino driven in from behind across the seam between the back leg's inner face and the seat's back edge; blind
seat.provenance: centre: the leg-side tip (|x| 199.55 triangulated, L/R mean; 199.35 as the mean of the single-photo readings on the left) minus half of the VISIBLE end (24.6 mm in the close-up IMG_1578; 25 to 26.5 in the distant photos, where the seat-side tip is soft) gives |x| 186.5 to 187.3; 186.8 taken. Section: fitted (24 x 10, as at the seat's side Dominos, parts/dominos.json: the visible end is the Domino plus a halo). Direction (square to the rear face) and depth (25 mm): ASSUMED, not visible
seat.note: the seat-side tip is the soft end: on IMG_1501 and 1502 the visible end runs 1 to 2 mm further into the seat than the model's (see observed.seat.visible_end_mm.seat_side_tip)

arm.kind: 10 mm Domino driven in from behind through the back leg into the end of the arm; its end shows on the leg's rear face
arm.provenance: centre: triangulated (L/R mean of the two ends' centres); section: fitted (visible end 23.1-23.5 x 10); direction (square to the rear face) and how far it runs into the arm (25 mm): ASSUMED, not visible
